title: Related GPU policy expressibility against the current gpubpf ABI
unit_of_classification: The paper's whole policy or system, not an isolated sub-heuristic.

observations: faulting page index and the current VA-block prefetch bounds
root-chunk activation and access events with owner/root/generation metadata
GPU task lifecycle and process identity in the separate scheduler ABI
actions: select one contiguous prefetch region inside the current VA block
reorder one root chunk to used/unused list head/tail
set a TSG timeslice and request supported whole-TSG preemption
important_absences: exact victim selection or direct eviction
page pinning, replication, remote mapping, or coherence control
DMA, network, queue, batch, or framework execution control
automatic model-layer, expert, token, or tensor semantic events

classification_definitions.FULL: The whole policy can be represented with the current observations and actions without changing its decision semantics.
classification_definitions.ANALOGUE: A useful policy with the same intent exists, but granularity or decision semantics differ materially.
classification_definitions.PARTIAL: One or more decision components map to current hooks, while named core actions or inputs are absent.
classification_definitions.NO: The paper's defining action is outside the current ABI; a similarly named local heuristic is not an implementation of the paper.

evidence_definitions.source: Primary paper/source was mapped to inspected in-tree source; no build or runtime claim.
evidence_definitions.build: The named local analogue also has a recorded successful build.
evidence_definitions.engagement: A real workload recorded that the named local analogue's hooks/actions engaged.
evidence_definitions.performance: A controlled run recorded an outcome metric for the named local analogue.

records.title: Towards High Performance Paged Memory for GPUs
observes: GPU page faults, access locality, and oversubscription pressure
acts: fault grouping, prefetching, and page eviction in a redesigned paging path
records.mapping_reason: Current hooks can replace the within-block prefetch choice and approximate recency ordering, but not the paper's full paging mechanism.

evidence.note: Literature-to-source mapping only; no reproduction claim.

records.title: Adaptive Page Migration for Irregular Data-intensive Applications under GPU Memory Oversubscription
observes: runtime access regularity and migration effectiveness
acts: adapts migration and prefetch behavior for irregular workloads
records.mapping_reason: Access-conditioned within-block prefetch is expressible, while migration destination and arbitrary-range control are not.

evidence.note: Source-level analogue assessment.

records.title: An Adaptive Framework for Oversubscription Management in CPU-GPU Unified Memory
observes: access-pattern class and oversubscription behavior
acts: selects and tunes prefetch and eviction behavior
records.mapping_reason: A bounded controller can choose local prefetch/reorder heuristics, but the ABI lacks the framework's full migration controls and telemetry.

evidence.note: Policy components mapped; original controller not ported.

records.title: A Framework for Memory Oversubscription Management in Graphics Processing Units
observes: application access-pattern class and reuse behavior
acts: selects zero-copy, prefetch, and eviction modes
records.mapping_reason: The classifier's output could parameterize a local policy, but zero-copy selection and global migration modes are outside the ABI.

evidence.note: Classifier-to-policy input is conceptual only.

records.title: DeepUM: Tensor Migration and Prefetching in Unified Memory
observes: tensor identity, operator sequence, and tensor liveness
acts: migrates and prefetches tensor ranges around operators
records.mapping_reason: Local reuse/stride prediction is available, but current hooks neither receive tensor/operator semantics nor migrate complete tensor ranges.

evidence.note: Only page-level predictors are analogous.

records.title: An Intelligent Framework for Oversubscription Management in CPU-GPU Unified Memory
observes: learned access-pattern class and predicted future pages
acts: page prefetch and pre-eviction from model predictions
records.mapping_reason: Predictions could be supplied through maps and within-block prefetch can be selected, but exact pre-eviction and arbitrary ranges are unavailable.

evidence.note: No learned model is claimed in-tree.

records.title: Interplay between Hardware Prefetcher and Page Eviction Policy in CPU-GPU Unified Virtual Memory
observes: fault density, prefetch usefulness, and eviction interaction
acts: coordinates page prefetch and pre-eviction policies
records.mapping_reason: No-prefetch and current-block prefetch subpolicies map directly, but coordinated pre-eviction and exact victims do not.

evidence.note: Whole-paper classification remains PARTIAL despite expressible subpolicies.

records.title: Page Placement Strategies for GPUs within Heterogeneous Memory Systems
observes: page access location, sharing, and heterogeneous-memory behavior
acts: chooses page placement among heterogeneous memories
records.mapping_reason: List reordering and an HBM prefetch bound do not choose a heterogeneous destination or maintain placement/coherence state.

evidence.note: Mechanism-level placement is not represented as an implemented policy.

records.title: Mosaic: A GPU Memory Manager with Application-Transparent Support for Multiple Page Sizes
observes: contiguity, page utilization, and translation pressure
acts: coalesces and splinters pages and manages multiple page sizes
records.mapping_reason: The current ABI neither changes page size nor controls physical allocation and address translation.

evidence.note: Mosaic is a memory-manager mechanism, not a current hook policy.

records.title: SUV: Static Analysis Guided Unified Virtual Memory
observes: compiler-derived thread-to-data working sets and runtime residency
acts: reserves HBM and performs proactive plus on-demand range migration
records.mapping_reason: A fault-local policy cannot reproduce compiler-derived whole working sets, HBM reservation, or proactive arbitrary-range migration.

evidence.note: Assessment uses the primary publication URL, not local mislabeled material.

records.title: DREAM: Device-Driven Efficient Access to Virtual Memory
observes: device-side misses and remote-memory access state
acts: uses GPU threads and an RDMA NIC to service virtual-memory access
records.mapping_reason: DREAM replaces the data path with device/NIC mechanisms; host UVM prefetch and list-reorder callbacks cannot express that path.

evidence.note: Mechanism replacement is deliberately not labeled a policy port.

records.title: Forest: Access-aware GPU UVM Management
observes: access patterns and data-object structure
acts: selects object-aware prefetch and migration behavior
records.mapping_reason: Access-aware local prefetch is representable, while object identity and cross-block tree/range actions are absent.

evidence.note: The local tree-named policy is a page-level analogue, not Forest reproduction.

records.title: HELM: Characterizing Unified Memory Accesses to Improve GPU Performance under Memory Oversubscription
observes: interpretable unified-memory access metrics
acts: selects a migration and placement policy from workload characteristics
records.mapping_reason: A userspace controller could configure an in-tree heuristic, but several HELM metrics and migration/placement actions are unavailable at the hooks.

evidence.note: Policy-selection feasibility only; no HELM model is implemented.

records.title: Towards MoE Deployment: Mitigating Inefficiencies in Mixture-of-Expert (MoE) Inference
observes: gating output, active/hot experts, and expert load
acts: changes gating, caches whole experts, and balances expert placement
records.mapping_reason: The tree contains a profile-guided page-granular hot-residency analogue; it is not expert-atomic buffering, dynamic gating, or load balancing.

evidence.note: Evidence covers only the explicitly bounded page-level analogue.

records.title: MoE-Infinity: Efficient MoE Inference on Personal Machines with Sparsity-Aware Expert Cache
observes: expert activation traces and cache reuse
acts: selects whole-expert replacement and prefetch
records.mapping_reason: Activation/fault history can guide page order and local prefetch, but the ABI lacks expert identity and whole-expert transfer.

evidence.note: Mapping does not claim MoE-Infinity's cache is reimplemented.

records.title: Fiddler: CPU-GPU Orchestration for Fast Inference of Mixture-of-Experts Models
observes: token routing, expert residency, and CPU/GPU compute cost
acts: places expert computation on CPU or GPU and overlaps execution
records.mapping_reason: The defining action is compute placement and orchestration, not a UVM prefetch or eviction-order decision.

evidence.note: No similarly named local memory heuristic is treated as Fiddler.

records.title: HOBBIT: A Mixed Precision Expert Offloading System for Fast MoE Inference
observes: token criticality, layer prediction, and sequence-level expert reuse
acts: loads precision variants, prefetches experts, and manages expert cache
records.mapping_reason: Reuse-guided page ordering approximates one cache component; precision selection and expert-atomic transfers remain framework actions.

evidence.note: Page-level component mapping only.

records.title: ProMoE: Fast MoE-based LLM Serving using Proactive Caching
observes: intermediate activations used to predict subsequent experts
acts: proactively transfers predicted whole experts into GPU cache
records.mapping_reason: A prediction can be communicated to policy maps, but current prefetch acts only on a bounded region during an existing UVM fault.

evidence.note: Local MoE prefetch is not ProMoE's proactive transfer pipeline.

records.title: PopFetcher: Learning-based Popularity-Aware Expert Prefetching for MoE
observes: expert popularity and distributed routing behavior
acts: prefetches experts across devices according to predicted popularity
records.mapping_reason: Popularity can approximate page protection, but peer expert pulls and distributed token/expert movement are absent.

evidence.note: Estimator intent maps only to an approximate page policy.

records.title: MoE-Lightning: High-Throughput MoE Inference on Memory-Constrained GPUs
observes: expert routing and end-to-end operator pipeline state
acts: co-schedules expert loading, CPU/GPU work, and the inference pipeline
records.mapping_reason: Its defining pipeline and compute orchestration cannot be expressed by bounded fault-time prefetch and chunk list ordering.

evidence.note: System-level mechanism is not labeled as an implemented policy.

records.title: FlexGen: High-Throughput Generative Inference of Large Language Models with a Single GPU
observes: model graph, tensor sizes, and latency/capacity cost model
acts: optimizes weight, activation, and KV placement across GPU, CPU, and disk
records.mapping_reason: The current ABI has neither tensor semantics nor CPU/disk tier and transfer scheduling actions.

evidence.note: FlexGen is a framework-level execution optimizer.

records.title: InfiniGen: Efficient Generative Inference of Large Language Models with Dynamic KV Cache Management
observes: attention semantics and predicted important KV entries
acts: selectively transfers and retains KV-cache entries
records.mapping_reason: UVM page faults do not expose token/head KV identity, and a contiguous page hint cannot implement selective KV entry transfer.

evidence.note: No KV-runtime reimplementation is claimed.

records.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
observes: request sequences, token blocks, reference counts, and sharing
acts: allocates, shares, and copy-on-writes logical KV blocks
records.mapping_reason: The driver callbacks cannot implement the runtime's logical KV allocator, sharing, or copy-on-write semantics.

evidence.note: gpubpf may complement vLLM UVM use; it does not implement PagedAttention.

records.title: PowerInfer: Fast Large Language Model Serving with a Consumer-grade GPU
observes: predicted neuron activation and model-layer semantics
acts: places and computes hot/cold neurons across GPU and CPU
records.mapping_reason: Neuron-level prediction and CPU/GPU operator dispatch are above the page-policy ABI.

evidence.note: A hot-page policy is not PowerInfer's neuron-level system.

records.title: ZeRO-Infinity: Breaking the GPU Memory Wall for Extreme Scale Deep Learning
observes: training graph, parameter/gradient/optimizer partitions, and topology
acts: partitions and offloads tensors through GPU, CPU, and NVMe tiers
records.mapping_reason: Distributed tensor partitioning and NVMe transfer pipelines are not page-reorder or current-block prefetch actions.

evidence.note: Whole-system training support is outside the ABI.

records.title: Capuchin: Tensor-based GPU Memory Management for Deep Learning
observes: tensor liveness, access order, and recomputation cost
acts: evicts, prefetches, or recomputes whole tensors
records.mapping_reason: Reuse ranking can approximate eviction order, but tensor liveness, exact range transfer, and recomputation are missing.

evidence.note: Only the ranking idea has a page-granular analogue.

records.title: GPREEMPT: GPU Preemptive Scheduling Made General and Efficient
observes: task priority, launch progress, and preemption state
acts: sets scheduling policy and performs yield-assisted pre-preemption
records.mapping_reason: In-tree programs implement priority timeslices and supported whole-TSG preemption intent, not GPREEMPT's yield and driver design.

evidence.note: This row claims policy-intent analogy, not artifact reproduction or performance parity.

records.title: GCAPS: GPU Context-Aware Preemptive Priority-Based Scheduling for Real-Time Tasks
observes: real-time task GPU segments, priorities, and context state
acts: admits and priority-preempts GPU contexts with schedulability guarantees
records.mapping_reason: Priority timeslice/preemption actions map, but GPU-segment annotations and real-time admission/guarantee machinery do not.

evidence.note: No real-time certification or GCAPS taskset reproduction is claimed.

records.title: XSched: Preemptive Scheduling for Diverse XPUs
observes: XQueue operations, command progress, and scheduling policy state
acts: queues, intercepts, suspends, and resumes work across XPU types
records.mapping_reason: GPU priority/timeslice intent maps, but the cross-XPU XQueue runtime and command-level resume model do not.

evidence.note: Only a scheduling-policy subset is mapped.

records.title: Microsecond-scale Preemption for Concurrent GPU-accelerated DNN Inferences
observes: kernel boundaries, DNN request priority, and execution progress
acts: kills/restores kernels and pads execution for microsecond preemption
records.mapping_reason: Whole-TSG preemption provides coarse priority control, not REEF's kernel kill/restore and padding mechanisms.

evidence.note: Coarser preemption is not REEF reproduction.

records.title: Fine-Grained GPU Sharing Primitives for Deep Learning Applications
observes: DL iteration boundaries and persistent/ephemeral memory demand
acts: lane scheduling and framework memory sharing at iteration granularity
records.mapping_reason: Per-process scheduling and memory priority are approximable, while iteration lanes and the framework allocator are absent.

evidence.note: Two coarse policy components, not Salus, are present.

records.title: Transparent GPU Sharing in Container Clouds for Deep Learning Workloads
observes: container submissions, feedback, and configured rates
acts: gates GPU submissions to enforce sharing rates
records.mapping_reason: Timeslices can bias service at process granularity, but the ABI cannot rate-gate each submission or reproduce TGS feedback control.

evidence.note: Timeslice control is only a coarse substitute.

records.title: G10: Enabling An Efficient Unified GPU Memory and Storage Architecture with Smart Tensor Migrations
observes: tensor lifetime, access schedule, and GPU/CPU/storage capacity
acts: plans and executes tensor migration across GPU memory and storage
records.mapping_reason: The current ABI cannot select storage as a destination or schedule tensor-range I/O.

evidence.note: Repository is a primary artifact; no G10 port is claimed.

records.title: Lina: Accelerating Distributed Mixture-of-Experts Model Training with Dynamic Scheduling
observes: MoE communication stages, network contention, and expert workload
acts: schedules computation and communication across distributed GPUs
records.mapping_reason: Local UVM and TSG hooks do not schedule collectives, token routing, or network traffic across nodes.

evidence.note: Distributed runtime control is outside scope.

records.title: Memory Harvesting in Multi-GPU Systems with Hierarchical Unified Virtual Memory
observes: per-GPU free capacity and hierarchical memory pressure
acts: harvests peer GPU memory and chooses hierarchical placement
records.mapping_reason: Current memory callbacks are local and expose neither peer capacity nor a peer destination action.

evidence.note: PID quota is not hierarchical multi-GPU placement.

records.title: GPS: A Global Publish-Subscribe Model for Multi-GPU Memory Management
observes: global page sharing, readers/writers, and replica state
acts: publishes, subscribes, replicates, and maintains page coherence
records.mapping_reason: Local list ordering cannot create replicas, route peer access, or enforce a global coherence protocol.

evidence.note: GPS requires a multi-GPU memory mechanism.

records.title: Combining HW/SW Mechanisms to Improve NUMA Performance of Multi-GPU Systems
observes: multi-GPU NUMA locality and cache behavior
acts: coordinates placement, remote caching, and coherence mechanisms
records.mapping_reason: The ABI lacks peer topology, remote-cache control, and coherence actions.

evidence.note: Hardware/software co-design is not a local reorder policy.

records.title: Griffin: Hardware-Software Support for Efficient Page Migration in Multi-GPU Systems
observes: per-GPU page locality, sharing, and migration benefit
acts: selects source/destination GPUs and performs peer page migration
records.mapping_reason: The current memory ABI is single-PMM and cannot name a peer GPU or issue an exact peer migration.

evidence.note: No multi-GPU migration claim.
